A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARS research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2 training and downstream evaluations, plus ResNet-18 experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a GPT-2 batch-size sensitivity study in Appendix E.7.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same gradient correction, clipping, momentum, preconditioning, and parameter updates. The MARS-approx procedure is also unchanged; revisions to theoretical explanations do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebText, FineWeb-Edu 100B, the same downstream language benchmarks, and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. The added batch-size study uses existing GPT-2/OpenWebText coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: AdamW, Lion, Muon, Shampoo where applicable, and OpenAI-Comm. checkpoints for FineWeb-Edu evaluations. The new batch-size study uses the established MARS-AdamW versus AdamW comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E.7 adds experiments with global batch sizes 240, 480, and 960 for 80,000 steps, holding other main-experiment hyperparameters fixed. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; constant-learning-rate and WSD experiments are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E4.justification: v3 adds batch-size sensitivity analysis in Appendix E.7/Figure 19. Existing exact-versus-approximate, gamma-sensitivity, and learning-rate-scheduler analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report base seed 5000 in Table 11. Neither adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty estimates; Figure 19 continues reporting loss curves without uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Figure 19 adds training and validation loss trajectories for three batch sizes, reporting lower losses for MARS-AdamW than AdamW and a larger gap at smaller batches. Corresponding benchmark values in Tables 1–9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.4/4.6 become B.5/B.6 with revised conditions, bound coefficients, and movement-term weighting changed from 1/eta_t^2 to 1/eta_t. The variance-recursion lemma gains a gamma-choice qualification and its proof is revised. The explicit Nesterov special-case derivation is replaced by a shorter comparison. These changes affect formal substance beyond relocation.

C1.justification: The unified framework, three optimizer instantiations, optimizer connections, and GPT-2 efficiency claims remain. The introduction's theoretical contribution bullet is removed, but convergence claims remain elsewhere. The norm-based T^(-1/3) rate emphasized in v3 was already acknowledged in v2's Theorem 4.4 footnote.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the batch-size results as supporting greater usefulness of variance reduction in small-batch, high-variance settings. Appendix B.2 also explicitly distinguishes the time-varying momentum parameters required by the analysis from the constants used in practice.

D1.justification: Appendix E.7 documents the new study's batch sizes, 80,000-step budget, and inheritance of other main-experiment hyperparameters. Existing hardware descriptions, Tables 10–12, and code availability remain unchanged; the repository link is relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds classical control-variate references and discussion of PROMISE, stochastic variance-reduced Newton, and VRAdam. It removes the Chen et al. (2018b) and Zhou et al. (2018) Adam-convergence references. These are limited updates to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 moves the Nesterov connection and theoretical analysis into Appendix B and learning-rate-scheduler studies into Appendix E.6. It rewrites the variance-control explanation, shortens the Nesterov discussion, adds an Impact Statement, and removes acknowledgments. The Lion connection derivation is also duplicated in the revised main text.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of algorithms, figures, and tables. Training-token axes are corrected from 0–5000 to 0–50 billion, CIFAR-100 accuracy axes previously labeled Test loss are corrected, and Figure 19 is added.

improvement.justification: The batch-size study and corrected plot axes improve empirical support and clarity. However, the revised theory introduces inconsistencies: v3's Eq. D.12 omits a beta factor when simplifying the optimal-gamma expression, unlike v2's compact expression in Remark 4.5. The revised theorem statements also use different movement-term normalizations from their proofs. These mathematical concerns prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the empirical and presentation gains.
